title: The 29 behested-payment waivers, the reports they promised, and the reports on file
question: Which waivers promised the Board a report of the donations solicited, when were those reports due, and which reports are attached to the Board files?
finding: Of the 29 waivers (5 in 2023, 4 in 2024, 16 in 2025, 4 in 2026), 19 carry a written promise to report donations to the Board, all of them from 2025 on; the reporting date had passed for 15 by 20 November 2026. Reports are attached to 5 Board files, and the Clerk's lists of communications to the Board record 3 more that are not in this project's files (Ordinance 010-25, listed 2026-02-13; Resolution 126-25, listed 2025-12-30; Resolution 569-25, listed 2026-06-24); 8 files whose reporting date has passed have no report on record. The reports read name 2 donors in all: The Prado Group, Inc., $51,000.00 for Downtown Development Corp. (File 251083); Fidelity Charitable Perspectives (Google), $1,000,000.00 for Breaking the Cycle (File 250754). The other three reports say no interested party was solicited. Late: File 250105 (Resolution 115-25) 91 days after the due date.
how: The DataSF waiver table (saved 20 Nov 2026) gives each file, enactment and approval date. Each enacted resolution is read for its reporting clause; the due date is the approval date plus six months plus 60 days (one month for the monthly clause), an approximation because a resolution can take effect on the Mayor's signature. Reports are the attachments named as waiver or behested-payment reports in the Legistar files saved the same day; their date is the date printed on them. The titles of the Clerk's communications files in the legislative record (saved 13-14 Nov 2026) are also searched for a waiver report sent under each resolution or ordinance number; those reports are counted as listed, not as read.
limits: The Clerk's communications titles were searched for a report sent under each resolution or ordinance number; a report listed under a title that does not give the number would still be missed, so an absence is a question for the Clerk, not proof that no report was made. A waiver is the Board's permission, and asking an interested party for a donation under a waiver is permitted. Reports cover only donors the office counts as interested parties; donations from others are reported to the Ethics Commission instead. Earlier waivers (2023-2024) did not ask for donor reports.
